item.title: Review: 'New Wave' Documentary Is a Surprisingly Personal Dissection of 1980s Nostalgia
item.description: Melodic synth-lines and steady electronic drums. Today, the signature sounds of new wave music feel perhaps a bit old and outdated. During its high point during the 1980s, however, new wave was hailed as music of the future. Vietnamese new wave, or new wave for short, is a genre of music that can be best described as Vietnamese American eurodisco. item.title: A Rare Album by Photographer Bruno Barbey Brings Us Back to Tết in 1994 Hanoi
item.description: What do you remember most about the 1990s? Do you remember the fashion, the old-timey technology, or the lack of traffic? And if you were just a wee child, do these memories stay with you? This collection of candid shots, taken by French photographer Bruno Barbey in Hanoi right during Tết of 1994 (Giáp Tuất), would teleport you to a simpler time of rudimentary new year decorations, sharp suits, and some particularly dope sunglasses. item.description: Plans for eventual metro access to the Long Thành International Airport are taking shape. item.title: From Dark to Dawn, an Early Morning at Hội An's Duy Hải Fish Market
item.description: At 3am, Hội An’s streets resemble dog-gnawed pork bones, licked clean of all scent and viscera. No light, no noise, no movement. But that’s the time you must venture out to witness the Duy Hải Fish Market in action. After you cross the Cửa Đại Bridge leading away from Old Town, you’ll turn into a warren of homes and notice the first signs of activity. item.title: A Brief History of Ông Đồ, Vietnam’s Scholars Whose Calligraphy Is Highly Sought After
item.description: To say that Tết gathers together everything most beautiful in Vietnamese culture would not be an exaggeration. More than a threshold between the old year and the new, it is also a time when people feel they can return to, and relive, the traditional values that define them. It is there in those year-end markets, where one searches for the familiar flavors of home. item.title: Hanoi Breaks Ground on Sports Complex With World's 2nd-Largest Stadium
item.description: Hanoi is currently building the country’s largest sports complex that’s hoped to become Vietnam’s go-to location to host international events and tournaments. On December 19, as Tuổi Trẻ reports, state officials broke ground on the Olympics Sports City at a 9,171-hectare patch of land south of Hanoi. item.title: Welcome to the New Age of Mass-Produced, Enshittified Plastic Bánh Giò
item.description: Do you always remember the first time you tried a new food? item.title: Life on the Streets of 1978 Hanoi, as Seen via Black-and-White Film Photos
item.description: In August 1978, I visited Hanoi as part of an educational tour organized by a professor from La Trobe University in Melbourne. I was a high school history teacher at the time and an avid photographer. I walked the streets of Hanoi and took many photographs of everyday life in the city, and until now, these photographs have remained unpublished. A pedicab driver seeking business in Đồng Xuân. item.title: Hẻm Gems: Bánh Canh Hẹ Is Phú Yên's Homage to Chives and the Sea
item.description: Ever since I was a kid, I have had a general dislike towards vegetables, but green onion has always been an exception. item.title: How Did Vietnam Start Celebrating International Women's Day on March 8?
